newsitem.title: CANADA: British Columbia looks to bolster Prince Rupert.
newsitem.headline: British Columbia looks to bolster Prince Rupert.

text.p: British Columbia said Friday it would explore ways to improve rail service to the port of Prince Rupert in hopes of increasing shipments.
Shipping delays at Canada's west coast ports have angered grain producers and other interest groups.

British Columbia minister for employment and investment Dan Miller said Canadian National Railway Co's sole ownership of the line between Prince George and Prince Rupert in the northwest created "impediments to increasing rail traffic."
Provincially-owned BC Rail also operates in northern British Columbia and Miller said there were several options which might help speed rail traffic to Prince Rupert.

These include potential purchase of the Prince George-Prince Rupert line by BC Rail and co-ownership of the line by the two railroads, Miller said. He also urged the railways to consider co-ownership of terminals in Prince Rupert.
Miller said he wrote to Paul Tellier, chief executive of CN Rail, and asked him to consider entering talks with BC Rail to pursue "these and other options."
